hero.title: A voice agent that lives on your hardware.
hero.subtitle: Talk to it and it answers out loud, in a voice and character you shape. It remembers you and acts through the skills you connect. No cloud, no accounts.
hero.imageAlt: Domia, the local voice agent character

converses.title: Talks with you
converses.body: Voice in, voice out. It listens, thinks and answers in its own voice, and follow-up mode keeps the microphone open so you can just keep talking.

acts.title: Acts through skills
acts.body: Built-in tools such as timers, alarms and reminders work from the first turn. Home Assistant, Music Assistant and any other MCP server join once you connect them in the console, and each can be switched off per Domia. Known commands run at once; for anything else the model decides whether to use a skill or just answer.

remembers.title: Remembers you
remembers.body: Recent turns, facts it learned, knowledge you write, episodes, and a model of who you are. All of it is stored on your node.

interrupt.title: Lets you interrupt
interrupt.body: Start speaking while it answers and the reply stops so it can hear you. On a satellite the reply pauses instead of cutting off.

consoleTeaser.title: A console for every node
consoleTeaser.body: Every node you run, in one place: who is online, what each one heard and said, and what it remembers. Apply a template or build a configuration from scratch, and edit routines, satellites and memories from the browser.
consoleTeaser.imageAlt: The console overview: fleet counters and a map of the Domias on the local mesh

why.title: Why it exists
why.p1: A voice agent hears more of your life than any other software. Something that close should run on a machine you can unplug: what it hears, remembers and learns stays there, and nobody else gets a copy.
why.p2: So Domia does the whole conversation on your hardware: it listens, thinks, speaks and acts through the skills you connect. Each Domia has its own name, voice and memory, and all three are yours to shape.

what.q: How is Domia different from a cloud assistant?
what.a: Domia is a voice agent that runs on hardware you own. It holds a conversation, remembers what you told it and acts through the skills you connect. Your voice is processed at home, there is no account, and you choose its name, voice and temperament.

privacy.a: They stay on your node. Audio, transcripts and memory are processed and stored on your hardware, and there is no account to sign in to. A skill you connect reaches only the service it controls.

cost.a: The software is free and open source under the Apache 2.0 license. You provide the hardware it runs on.

hardware.q: What do I need to run it?
hardware.a: A machine you own, a microphone and a speaker. A thin device covers a room and delegates the heavy work; a capable machine runs every stage itself; a hub-class machine serves several rooms. Domia adapts to your hardware.

offline.a: Yes. Listening, understanding, the model and the spoken reply all run on your network, so conversation, memory and built-in tools keep working. Skills keep working when the service they control is also local; anything that lives in the cloud, such as a streaming provider, stops until the connection returns.

rooms.q: Does it work in several rooms?
rooms.a: Yes. One hub can serve a Domia per room, each with its own name and voice, through a satellite in each room. Announcing something to every room, or opening an intercom between two, is done from the console's Broadcast page, not by voice.

internet.q: Can I reach it from outside my home?
internet.a: Do not expose a node to the internet: there is no per-user authentication. Keep it on your home network and use a VPN when you are away.

smartHome.a: Yes, through the skills you connect; Home Assistant and Music Assistant are the providers tested every day. A known command takes the fast path and calls the skill directly. For anything else the model gets a shortlist of fitting skills and decides whether to call one or just answer.

homeAssistant.q: Does it work without Home Assistant?
homeAssistant.a: Yes. Conversation, memory, the knowledge base and built-in tools such as timers, alarms, reminders and routines need nothing else. Home Assistant and Music Assistant add the house: lights, scenes, media and whatever else you expose to them.

skills.q: How do I add a skill?
skills.a: Built-in tools such as timers, alarms and reminders work from the first turn. Other skills connect over MCP: in the console, open the Skills section of a Domia's configuration and connect an MCP server, such as Home Assistant or Music Assistant, and its tools start working. Each skill has a policy (allow, ask first or block) that you set per identity, so you can switch any of them off.

guests.a: They just talk to it. You write the knowledge base (wifi, house rules, meal times, phone numbers, local picks) and Domia answers from it. It answers only what you wrote; there is no web search.

interrupt.a: Yes. Talk over the reply and it stops and listens. On a satellite the reply pauses instead of cutting off.

memoryLayers.title: Memory: what Domia remembers
memoryLayers.intro: Five layers, all kept on the node. All of them can reach the prompt: recent turns always, facts and knowledge when they are relevant, episodes and the user model once per session. Reflection writes facts, episodes and the user model when it is idle.

pills.inPromptSession: in the prompt, once per session

recentTurns.name: Recent turns
recentTurns.description: The last exchanges, in the prompt.
recentTurns.example: "And the kitchen too." Domia knows which light you mean.
recentTurns.hint: A rolling window of the latest exchanges from the current session. It is always in the prompt, so a follow-up resolves without repeating yourself.

facts.name: Facts
facts.description: Things you told it, in the prompt when relevant.
facts.example: "The dog is called Nala and sleeps in the kitchen."
facts.hint: Extracted after the turn by a reflection pass in the background, never by the reply itself. Recalled by relevance to what you just said.

knowledge.name: Knowledge base
knowledge.description: What you wrote for it (wifi, house rules), in the prompt when relevant.
knowledge.example: "Guest wifi is casa-guest. Bins go out on Tuesday night."
knowledge.hint: Notes you author in the console or through the API. They are searched by relevance and added to the prompt when they match the request.

episodes.name: Episodes
episodes.description: Summaries of past sessions, in the prompt once per session.
episodes.example: "Last week you planned a dinner for six and asked for a shopping list."
episodes.hint: A short summary written by reflection once a session ends. The latest ones are loaded into the prompt once per session, not searched on every turn.

userModel.name: User model
userModel.description: Who you are to it: interests, habits and how familiar you are.
userModel.example: "Prefers short answers and no small talk."
userModel.hint: A short picture of you: interests, tendencies and preferences. Reflection updates it between sessions.

memoryLayers.footer: Everything stays on the node. Nothing is persisted on a peer; context travels inside a delegated request.
memoryLayers.link: See the Memories screen in the console

localPipeline.label: Local voice pipeline
localPipeline.note: Wake word, speech to text, the language model and text to speech all run on your hardware.

fastPath.label: Fast path
fastPath.note: A known command matches a template and calls the skill directly, without the language model. Locks, alarm panels and sirens never take this path.

builtinTools.label: Built-in tools
builtinTools.note: Time, date, timers, alarms, reminders, volume, remember and forget work with no provider connected; timers, alarms and reminders survive a restart.

mcpSkills.label: Skills over MCP
mcpSkills.note: Any MCP server adds its tools as skills, and each one can be allowed, asked first or blocked. Home Assistant and Music Assistant are the providers tested every day.

routines.label: Routines
routines.note: Short multi-step sequences with a single spoken reply.

satelliteProtocols.label: Four satellite protocols
satelliteProtocols.note: Home Assistant Voice PE, Wyoming satellites, browser rooms and your own boards, all behind one contract.

realtimeEndpoint.label: Endpoint for Realtime apps
realtimeEndpoint.note: Apps that speak the OpenAI Realtime API can use Domia as their local backend.

memoryLayers.label: Five memory layers
memoryLayers.note: Recent turns, facts, knowledge base, episodes and a user model.

console.label: Console
console.note: Fleet, live configuration, templates, satellites, broadcast, routines, conversation replay, memories, emotions and analytics.

mindTransfer.label: Export and import a Domia
mindTransfer.note: Character, mood, memories, knowledge, routines, satellites and skills move as one bundle, with credentials stripped.

smallModelReplyQuality.label: Reply quality on small models
smallModelReplyQuality.note: The voice pipeline is stable; how good the replies are on small models is still being tuned.

poolJobCancellation.label: Stopping speech already in progress
poolJobCancellation.note: Interrupting stops new work at once; cancelling a sentence that is already being synthesized is pending.

ci.label: Automated test pipeline
ci.note: Tests and benchmarks exist and are run by hand; nothing runs them automatically yet.

proactiveNudges.label: Domia speaking first
proactiveNudges.note: Built, off by default: when the house is quiet it can offer a short, rate-limited nudge instead of waiting for a wake word.

bargeIn.label: Barge-in and follow-up
bargeIn.note: Talk over a reply and it stops; after a reply the microphone stays open for your next sentence.

identityMood.label: Identity and mood
identityMood.note: Each Domia has its own name, voice, temperament and a mood across eight emotion axes that shades how it speaks.

mesh.label: Mesh and delegation
mesh.note: Nodes find each other and a thin device hands speech, language or voice work to a capable machine, keeping its own identity.

multiIdentity.label: Several identities per node
multiIdentity.note: One machine can host a Domia per room, each with its own memory and satellites.

meshSecurity.label: Mesh secret and rotation
meshSecurity.note: A shared secret between nodes is required; encrypted transport is optional, and the secret can be rotated without cutting nodes off.

broadcast.label: Broadcast and intercom
broadcast.note: From the console, announce to one room or all of them, or open a live voice link between two rooms.

speakerRecognition.label: Recognising who is speaking
speakerRecognition.note: Domia does not tell voices apart yet; everyone in the room is the same person to it.

remoteAccess.label: Per-user accounts and remote access
remoteAccess.note: Nodes are guarded by a shared secret, but there are no per-user accounts yet, so a node must stay on your own network and never be exposed to the internet.

automaticUpdates.label: Automatic updates
automaticUpdates.note: Updating a node is a manual step.

voicePath.title: Where does your voice go?
voicePath.intro: With Domia the whole turn runs on a machine you own, so audio, transcripts and memory never reach a third party.
voicePath.offlineNote: the cloud side stops answering; Domia keeps working
voicePath.note: Everything on your network keeps working: lights, speakers, your knowledge base. Only services that live in the cloud, like a streaming provider, need the internet.

pipeline.title: The voice pipeline: one spoken turn
pipeline.intro: The stages overlap: Domia starts speaking while the model is still writing.
pipeline.stageLabel: Timeline of one spoken turn across eight lanes, from your voice to the reply you hear
pipeline.headline: It starts talking about {halves, select, 1 {half a second} 2 {a second} 3 {a second and a half} other {{seconds} seconds}} after you stop.

mic.label: You speak
mic.note: captured on the device until you pause
mic.tip: The wake word and voice activity detection run on the device; your speech is captured until a pause is detected.

stt.label: It understands
stt.tip: Text arrives while you are still talking, so the final transcript is ready right after the end of speech.

routing.label: It decides
routing.note: a known command runs at once; otherwise the model picks a skill or answers
routing.tip: Each turn first tries the command templates your skills bring. If none matches, the model receives the skills that fit the request and decides whether to call one or answer.

mind.label: building the mind
mind.tip: The prompt is assembled from the persona, the current mood, facts about you, your knowledge base and the last turns; once per session it also carries past episodes and a short picture of you.

llm.label: It thinks
llm.tip: Words stream out as they are generated; the sentence splitter reads them as they arrive.

splitter.label: sentence splitter
splitter.tip: As soon as a sentence is complete it is handed to text to speech, while the model keeps writing the next one.

tts.label: It talks
tts.tip: Each sentence is synthesised on its own, so the first one can play while the others are still being generated.

hear.label: You hear it
hear.tip: Playback starts with the first sentence; the rest queue behind it without gaps.

endOfSpeech.title: end of speech detected
endOfSpeech.note: silence + a small turn model agree

firstAudio.title: first sound
firstAudio.note: ≈ {seconds} s after your last word on {machine}

checkpoints.llm: otherwise → the model, with the skills that fit

epilogue.micReopen: the mic re-opens: just answer, no wake word
epilogue.reflectionBody: updates mood and remembers new facts
epilogue.bargeIn: Talk over it and it stops and listens.

caveats.pingWatchdog: The node notices when a device stops answering.
caveats.nodeConnectsOut: The node opens the connection, so the satellite needs an address the node can reach.
caveats.noPlaybackConfirmation: Wyoming sends no playback confirmation, so the node is not told when a reply finished playing.
caveats.needsRuntimeOnNode: Browser rooms need an extra component installed on the node; platforms without it skip this kind of satellite.
caveats.webrtcRoom: Audio travels through a room that any browser or app can join.
caveats.referenceProtocol: The reference design: every other kind of satellite behaves the same way once connected.
caveats.diyBuild: Bring your own capture, wake word and playback; the node handles the rest.

home.title: At home
home.intro: A day in a house with Domia, from the alarm to good night.
home.needs: What you need: one capable machine with a microphone and a speaker. Lights need Home Assistant, music needs Music Assistant, and more rooms need satellites. Conversation, memory, timers, alarms and reminders need nothing else.

hospitality.title: Hosting guests
hospitality.intro: A use case the knowledge base makes possible. You write what guests usually ask, and the room answers by voice. It answers only what you wrote. Each room's Domia speaks with the name, voice and temperament you choose, so it sounds like your place.

also.title: Also in the house
also.identities: Several Domias can live on one machine, each with its own name, voice and memory.
also.broadcast: From the console's Broadcast page you can send an announcement to every room, or open an intercom between two.
also.move: A Domia can move to another machine with everything it knows.

notes.title: Write the notes
notes.body: In the console, add short entries: wifi, house rules, check-out, meal times, phone numbers, your local picks.

hub.title: Run one hub
hub.body: A hub-class machine on the property does the listening, the thinking and the speaking for every room.

rooms.title: Give each room a Domia
rooms.body: A satellite in the room and its own Domia, with a name, a voice and its own notes.

limits.title: What it will not do
limits.body: It has no web search: what you did not write, it cannot look up. For guest rooms you can switch off memory for that room's Domia, so what one guest tells it is not remembered for the next.

alarm.happens: A known command, so the built-in alarm is set without the model. Alarms, timers and reminders are built in: there is nothing to connect.

companion.happens: No command here, so the model just answers, in the character and voice you gave it. When things are quiet it looks back on the conversation, and its mood follows.

followUp.happens: After a reply the microphone stays open for a moment, so the next sentence needs no wake word. Repeating is a known command.

memory.line: How do I take my coffee?
memory.happens: You said it once, or asked it to remember. Facts about you stay on your node, and you can read and delete them in the console.

lights.happens: A known command: it goes straight to Home Assistant without waiting for the model.

music.line: Play some jazz in the living room.
music.happens: Not a fixed phrase, so the model picks the Music Assistant skill and fills in what to play and where. Pause, skip and volume are known commands and skip the model.

timer.line: Set a timer for twenty minutes.
timer.happens: The timer is stored on the node: it survives a restart and never rings twice.

reminder.line: Remind me to take my pills at nine.
reminder.happens: Free words and a time, so the model fills in the reminder and the built-in skill stores it. It is spoken aloud at nine.

bargeIn.happens: Talk over it and it stops; on a satellite the reply pauses while you speak. Cancelling is a known command, so it just says okay.

goodnight.happens: A routine you define in the console: lights off, music off, alarm set. Its phrase becomes a known command; it runs the steps in order and answers once.

wifi.happens: You write the wifi, the house rules and the check-out time once. Every guest gets the answer by voice, and nothing leaves the property.

readingLight.happens: With Home Assistant in the property it is a known command: the reading light turns on without waiting for the model.

mealTimes.happens: Meal times, pool hours and quiet hours are notes. Change one in the console and the room answers with the new time.

nearby.line: Any good places to eat nearby?
nearby.happens: It recommends the places you wrote down, in your own words. It does not search the web.

frontDesk.line: What's the number for the front desk?
frontDesk.happens: Phone numbers, and who to call for what, are in the same notes, ready at any hour.

time.happens: The built-in clock answers at once, with nothing to connect and no internet needed.
